question.prompt: A boat travels \(12\) kilometers perpendicularly away from the shore, then travels \(5\) kilometers in a perpendicular direction. What is its straight-line distance from the starting point, in kilometers?

solutions.explanation:
Under the recorded interpretation that the second travel leg is perpendicular to the first, the straight-line distance is the hypotenuse of a right triangle. By the Pythagorean theorem, it is
\[
\sqrt{12^2+5^2}=\sqrt{169}=13\text{ km}.
\]
The wording does not explicitly say what the second direction is perpendicular to. If it is again perpendicular to the shore, continuing away gives \(12+5=17\) km, while returning toward the shore gives \(12-5=7\) km. Thus the recorded answer is \(13\) km under its stated interpretation, but the wording alone does not determine a unique distance.
solutions.title: Conditional right-triangle model
